input:
Write a bash script that generates an HTML page from settings. Starting files: --- /home/eval/site.env --- TITLE=Release Notes VERSION=2.4.1 --- end --- Note the values are not shell-quoted (TITLE contains a space). Create /home/eval/site/index.html (the directory does not exist) whose content is exactly the following, where `Release Notes` and `2.4.1` come from TITLE and VERSION in site.env, and the two lines inside `
` appear literally, character for character (no expansion):
```

Release Notes 2.4.1


Release Notes


Version 2.4.1


export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH"
echo "built: $(date +%F)"




```
Exit 0.

transcript.final_response:
The script parses site.env without sourcing it, because the values aren't shell-quoted. It then writes the HTML with a quoted here-doc for the literal part and `printf` for the parts that come from the settings. ```bash #!/bin/bash set -e envfile=/home/eval/site.env TITLE="" VERSION="" while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do line="${line%$'\r'}" case "$line" in TITLE=*) TITLE="${line#TITLE=}" ;; VERSION=*) VERSION="${line#VERSION=}" ;; esac done < "$envfile" mkdir -p /home/eval/site out=/home/eval/site/index.html { printf '\n' printf '%s %s\n' "$TITLE" "$VERSION" printf '\n' printf '

%s

\n' "$TITLE" printf '

Version %s

\n' "$VERSION" cat <<'EOF' 
export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH"
echo "built: $(date +%F)"
EOF } > "$out" exit 0 ```
